description: Test set for Basic vs Advanced RAG over the OpenCog/iCog corpus. Covers the four categories required by the assignment: simple factual, different-wording (paraphrase), multi-step/relationship, and answer-unavailable.

questions.question: In which city and country is iCog Labs located?
What does the acronym MORK stand for?
Which minimum version of SWI-Prolog does PeTTa require?
Which language is used to read from and write to the knowledge store in Hyperon, replacing the older Atomese?
What mechanism decides which pieces of knowledge the system should focus its limited resources on, and how does it model that decision?
questions.gold: ECAN (Economic Attention Networks), which spreads attention values (STI/LTI) using an economic model where attention is a limited currency

questions.question: Whose PhD research are the core ideas behind the MOSES program learner based on?
questions.gold: Moshe Looks (2006 PhD thesis 'Competent Program Evolution')

questions.question: How does the OmegaClaw agent keep memories over long periods of time?
questions.gold: Embedding-based long-term memory stored in the AtomSpace as (timestamp, atom, embedding) triplets, managed with remember/query/episodes/pin operations

questions.question: The person who founded SingularityNET also co-founded which Ethiopian AI company, and in what city is that company based?
questions.gold: Ben Goertzel founded SingularityNET and co-founded iCog Labs, which is based in Addis Ababa

questions.question: How are PeTTa and MORK related?
questions.gold: PeTTa uses MORK (via the mork_ffi bindings) to provide high-performance MORK-based atom spaces

questions.question: metta-moses is written in which MeTTa implementation, and what abstract machine does that implementation run on?
questions.gold: metta-moses is written in MeTTaLog, which runs on the Warren Abstract Machine (WAM) via SWI-Prolog

questions.question: Which reasoning component draws inferences using the truth values attached to atoms in the AtomSpace?
OmegaClaw keeps its long-term memory in a particular data structure; which high-performance kernel gives that same structure fast, scalable storage, and what does that kernel's name stand for?
questions.gold: OmegaClaw stores its long-term memory in the AtomSpace; MORK, which stands for MeTTa Optimal Reduction Kernel, gives the AtomSpace fast, scalable storage.

questions.question: metta-moses reimplements an earlier OpenCog program learner; what is that learner called and whose 2006 PhD thesis are its core ideas derived from?
questions.gold: metta-moses reimplements MOSES, whose core ideas are derived from Moshe Looks' 2006 PhD thesis 'Competent Program Evolution'.

questions.question: PeTTa implements a language whose programs run against a core knowledge store; which kernel accelerates that store for billions of atoms and what does its acronym stand for?
questions.gold: PeTTa implements MeTTa, which operates on the AtomSpace; MORK (MeTTa Optimal Reduction Kernel) accelerates that store so it scales to billions of atoms.

questions.question: How many full-time employees does iCog Labs currently have?
questions.gold: Not stated in the corpus - the system should refuse.

questions.question: What is the current market price of the SingularityNET (AGIX) token?
questions.gold: Not stated in the corpus - the system should refuse.

questions.question: In which exact year was the MeTTa language first officially released to the public?
questions.gold: Not stated in the corpus - the system should refuse.
